The *Kusalattika* (Patthana 7.1) is an Abhidhamma text situated within the *Paṭṭhāna* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. While the title designates the wholesome triad (*kusala-ttika*), the secondary literature provided in the dossier does not specifically analyze this seventh division, instead focusing on the opening *Kusalattika* of the *Tikapaṭṭhāna* (Patthana 1) or other compound triad configurations.

The largest reuse correspondences occur with other *Paṭṭhāna* sections treating the wholesome triad, particularly the *Kusalattika* of Patthana 1.2 (167 matches, 32,213 characters; longest shared passage §14.1–17.1_3 ↔ §768.1_17–773.1_0), *Kusalattika* of Patthana 19.1 (73 matches, 22,055 characters), *Kusalattika* of Patthana 13.1 (73 matches, 20,315 characters), and *Kusalattika, Tika* of Patthana 5.1 (69 matches, 15,831 characters) [DharmaNexus]. Additional substantial alignments appear with *Kusalattika, Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 4.3; 59 matches), *Nikkhepavāra* (Patthana 1.1; 46 matches), and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Abhidhammapiṭaka* (48 matches) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral does not record any curated parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit for this text [SuttaCentral].
